This city and the inhabitants thereof are hereby constituted and declared a body politic
               and corporate under the name and style Aragon, Georgia, and by that name shall have
               perpetual succession.

(a) The boundaries of this city shall be those existing on the effective date of the adoption
               of this Charter with such alterations as may be made from time to time in the manner
               provided by law. The boundaries of this city at all times shall be shown on a map,
               a written description or any combination thereof, to be retained permanently in the
               office of the City Clerk and to be designated, as the case may be: "Official Map of
               the corporate limits of the City of Aragon, Georgia." Photographic, typed, or other
               copies of such map or description certified by the City Clerk shall be admitted as
               evidence in all courts and shall have the same force and effect as with the original
               map or description. (b) The Mayor and City Council may provide for the redrawing of any such map by ordinance
               to reflect lawful changes in the corporate boundaries. A redrawn map shall supersede
               for all purposes the entire map or maps, which it is designated to replace.

(a) This city shall have all powers possible for a city to have under the present or future
               constitution and laws of this state as fully and completely as though they were specifically
               enumerated in this charter. This city shall have all the powers of self-government
               not otherwise prohibited by this charter or by general law. (b) The powers of this city shall be construed liberally in favor of the city. The specific
               mention [of] or failure to mention particular powers shall not be construed as limiting
               in any way the powers of this city.

The powers of the government of the City of…

questions.prompt: Is it against the law to drive a tractor with lugs on Auburn’s paved streets?
choices: No, farm equipment is always allowed
Only if the tractor is wider than a car
No, as long as you pay for any pavement damage
questions.excerpt:
Chapters:

Sections:

Pursuant to OCGA Sections 40-6-372, 40-1-1 through 40-1-5 and 40-6-1 through 40-6-395,
               known as the Uniform Rules of the Road, are adopted as and for the traffic regulations
               of the city, as though fully set forth in this chapter. (Ord. 246 (part), 1998)

Unless another penalty is expressly provided by law, any person convicted of a violation
               of any provision of the OCGA sections stated in Section 10.05.010 shall be punished
               by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars or imprisonment for not more than
               one hundred eighty days or by both such fine and imprisonment. (Ord. 246 (part), 1998)

All citations issued within the corporate limits of the city shall be returned to
               the city for adjudication. (Ord. 246 (part), 1998)

Sections:

It is unlawful for any person or persons to drive a tractor with lugs on the streets
               that are paved in the city or haul any equipment of any type that would disrupt or
               destroy the pavement of corporate limits of the city in any manner. Any person found
               guilty shall replace, repair or be responsible for the repair and be tried and fined
               as prescribed by ordinance. (Ord. 16, 1963)

Sections:

No person in charge of or in control of premises, whether as owner, lessee, tenant,
               occupant or otherwise, shall allow any more than one partially dismantled, wrecked,
               junked, discarded or otherwise non-operating motor vehicles to remain on such property.
               This chapter shall further not apply with regard to any vehicle in an appropriate
               storage place or depository maintained in a lawful place and manner by the city or
               any other public agency or commercial entity. (Ord. 261 (part), 2000) (Ord. No. 19-003, 7-2-19)

questions.prompt: Is it against Brooklet rules to leave barrels, boxes, or a vehicle on a street or sidewalk so people cannot easily pass?
choices: No, as long as you move them by morning
Yes, it is unlawful if passage is impeded
Only vehicles are banned, not boxes
questions.answer: Yes, it is unlawful if passage is impeded
questions.excerpt:
(a) Unlawful. No person shall place any lumber or timber, or leave any vehicle, barrels or boxes
               or any other obstruction in or on any of the streets or sidewalks of the city, so
               that passage thereon is impeded. (b) Necessary obstructions; regulations. (1) Permit required; scope. Whenever it shall become absolutely necessary for any one to obstruct said streets
               or sidewalks, or any part thereof, permission shall first be obtained from the mayor
               who shall under no circumstances grant a permit to obstruct more than one-half the
               width and not over 100 feet of length of said street. If the obstruction desired is
               a sidewalk, the mayor shall, if he thinks the circumstances require it, grant a permit
               to obstruct all of said sidewalk in width, but not more than 100 feet in length. (2) Barricade and lights required. Each person to whom said permit is granted shall keep at each end of said obstruction
               from sundown to sunup, a proper barricade and a lighted lantern or lanterns, the light
               therefrom to be sufficient to make the obstruction plainly visible. (Code 1986, §§ 13-1, 13-2)

No fence or ditch shall be erected or dug on the line of any street or sidewalk in
               the city without obtaining a permit from the mayor. (Code 1986, § 13-3)

No one shall erect any telephone or telegraph poles on the streets or sidewalks of
               the city without first obtaining a permit from the mayor. (Code 1986, § 13-4)

               or hereafter authorized to set poles for the stringing of wires thereon, upon notice
               from the mayor and council to that effect, to remove or reset any poles belonging
               to such company,…

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcohol means any ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl, or spirits of wine, from whatever
               source or by whatever process produced. Alcoholic beverage includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage, wine or fortified wine
               as defined in this section. Alcoholic beverage caterer means any retail dealer licensed pursuant to this chapter who provides alcohol at
               authorized events or functions, special events, or special events facilities. Authorized catered function means an event at a location not otherwise licensed for consumption of alcoholic
               beverages by the drink at which alcoholic beverages are furnished, for consideration,

               the drink, pursuant to a permit obtained under this chapter. Beer or malt beverage means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction
               of barley, malt, hops, or any other product, or any combination of such products in
               water containing not more than six percent alcohol by volume, and including ale, porter,
               brown, stout, lager beer, small beer, and strong beer. Also included are beverages
               known as nonalcoholic beer which is made by fermentation of any infusion or decoction
               of barley, malt, hops, or other products, and containing less than three percent,
               but more than 0.1 percent alcohol by volume. The term "malt beverage" does not include
               sake, known as Japanese rice wine. Brown bagging means the practice of customers, patrons, or guests bringing alcoholic beverages
               into an establishment or area…

questions.prompt: In Cook County, selling alcoholic beverages is treated as which of the following?
choices: A right every business can claim
A privilege the county can grant, not a right
questions.answer: A privilege the county can grant, not a right
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 22. State Law reference— Georgia Alcoholic Beverage Code, O.C.G.A. § 3-1-1 et seq.

(a) The purposes of this chapter shall include without being limited to the following: (1) Compliance with and effectuation of the general state law; (2) Prevention and control of the sale of alcoholic beverages by unfit persons; (3) Ensuring that any licenses issued for the consumption of alcoholic beverages are issued
               only as defined and set forth in this chapter; (4) The protection of schools, homes, churches, parks and other institutions; and (5) Protection of the public health, safety and welfare. (b) To the maximum extent possible under state and federal law, the business of selling
               alcoholic beverages shall under this chapter be considered a privilege to be afforded
               in conformity with subsection (a) of this section and other public policies of the
               county, rather than a right. (Ord. of 1-19-2007, intro.)

(a) The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcoholic beverage means and includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverages, wine or
               fortified wine. Brown bagging means the bringing of alcoholic beverages into restaurants or other business establishments
               or public places for the purpose of drinking such alcoholic beverages at any such
               establishment. Commercial recreational plantation: A large commercial farm property which, as its principal business model, for a fee
               allows customers to enjoy the natural and recreational attributes of the property,
               including, but not limited to, hunting, shooting, fishing, birding, hiking, horse-back
               riding, etc. For the purposes of this ordinance, a…

               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcohol means ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl, or spirits of wine, from whatever source
               or by whatever process produced. Alcoholic beverage includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, malt beverages, wine, or fortified wine
               as defined in this section. Bar means any establishment that is devoted to the serving of alcoholic beverages for
               consumption by guests on the premises and in which the serving of food is only incidental
               to the consumption of those beverages, including, but not limited to, taverns, nightclubs,
               cocktail lounges and cabarets. Beer means any malt beverage. Distilled spirits means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 21
               percent alcohol by volume, including but not limited to all fortified wines. Fortified wine means any alcoholic beverage containing more than 21 percent alcohol by volume made
               from fruits, berries or grapes, either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation
               with brandy added. Fortified wine includes but is not limited to brandy. Malt beverage means any alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction
               of barley, malt, hops, or any other similar product or any combination of such products
               in water, containing not more than six percent alcohol by volume, and including ale,
               porter, brown, stout, lager beer, malt beer, and strong beer, but not including sake,
               known as Japanese rice wine. Manufacturer means any maker, producer, distiller, brewer, vintner, rectifier, blender or bottler
               of an alcoholic beverage. Package means a bottle, can, keg, barrel or other…

questions.prompt: In DeKalb County, an animal is considered abandoned if it has been left unattended without adequate food and water for more than:
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 15-09 , Pt. I, adopted Dec. 15, 2015, repealed the former Ch. 5, §§ 5-1—5-28, and enacted
               a new Ch. 5 to read as set out herein. The former Ch. 5 pertained to similar subject
               matter and derived from Ord. No. 04-15, Pt. I, adopted Dec. 14, 2004; Ord. No. 05-01,
               Pt. I, adopted Jan. 25, 2005; Ord. No. 05-08, Pt. I, adopted July 12, 2005; and Ord.
               No. 13-02, Pt. I, adopted Jan. 22, 2013. Cross reference— Rabies control, § 13-126 et seq.

For the purposes of this chapter, certain terms and words are hereby defined. Where
               words or terms are not herein defined, but are defined in section 1-2 or other applicable sections of this Code or state law, now and as they may be amended
               hereafter, those words shall have the meaning as defined therein. As used in this
               chapter, unless the context otherwise indicates, the following words and terms shall
               have the meaning ascribed to them: Abandonment means the intentional or complete forsaking of any animal by its owner, without making
               reasonable arrangements for the adequate care and custody of the animal to be assumed
               by another person or the failure to return and resume responsibility of an animal
               at the designated time as arranged with the care giver. Abandonment also means the
               act of placing an animal on public property or within a public building, unattended
               or uncared for, or on or within the private property of another without the express
               permission of the owner, custodian or tenant of the private property. An animal shall
               also be considered abandoned when it has been unattended and without adequate and
               proper food and water for a period in excess of thirty-six (36) hours, regardless
               of where such animal may be found or kept.…

Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Georgia Alcoholic Beverage Code, O.C.G.A. § 3-1-1 et seq.; local regulation of alcoholic
               beverages, O.C.G.A. § 3-3-2; malt beverages, O.C.G.A. § 3-5-1 et seq.; wine, O.C.G.A.
               § 3-6-1 et seq.

The following words, terms, or phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcoholic beverage means and includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverage, wine or fortified
               wine as further defined in this chapter. Brown bagging means possession of an open glass bottle, can, or other container containing an alcoholic
               beverage or consumption of an alcoholic beverage on premises: (1) For which a city business license has been issued; and (2) Which occurs at a location different from where said alcoholic beverage was purchased. City manager means the city manager of the City of Demorest, Georgia. Distilled spirits means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 21
               percent alcohol by volume including, but not limited to, all fortified wines. Election day means that period of time beginning with the opening of the polls and ending with
               the closing of the polls. As used in this section, the term "election" is defined
               as any statewide primary election and the statewide general election and any runoff
               held for such primary or general election. The term also includes "local elections"
               in which the citizens of the city or any portion thereof vote either as residents

questions.prompt: In Douglas, an animal is considered abandoned if it sits unattended without enough food, water, ventilation, or shelter for longer than:
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Animals generally, O.C.G.A. title 4.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Abandon means the act of placing an animal on public property or within a public building,
               unattended or uncared for, or on or within the private property of another without
               the express permission of the owner, custodian, or tenant of the private property.
               An animal shall also be considered abandoned when it has been unattended and without
               adequate food, water, ventilation or shelter, for a period in excess of 36 hours,
               regardless of where such animal may be found or kept. Adequate food means sufficient quantity of non-contaminated and nutritionally healthy sustenance
               that is appropriate to the species, breed, size, age, and health of the animal, or
               at the direction of a licensed veterinarian, which is sufficient to prevent starvation,
               malnutrition, or risk to the animal's health. Garbage, spoiled, rancid, or contaminated
               food is not adequate food. Adequate shelter means a protective covering for an animal that is of adequate size and provides adequate
               protection to maintain the animal in a state of good health, and that prevents pain,
               suffering, or significant risk to the animal's health. Adequate shelter shall consist
               of a completely enclosed structure with four sides with a door opening, a constructed
               floor, and a roof. It should also be clean, dry, and compatible with current weather
               conditions, in addition to age, size, species, and condition of the animal. The structure
               should be of sufficient size to allow the animal to stand, turn around,…

questions.prompt: In Echols County, when may you leave a dead dog on someone else’s private property?

Only after you get the property owner’s permission and follow state law
If you bury it the same day
questions.answer: Only after you get the property owner’s permission and follow state law
questions.excerpt:
(a) Upon private property. No person shall intentionally abandon a dead dog on any private property belonging
               to another unless the person so doing shall have first obtained permission from the
               owner of the property on which the dog is being left and the provisions of O.C.G.A.
               § 4-5-3 are complied with in full. (b) Upon public property. No person shall abandon a dead dog on any public property or public right-of-way
               unless the place in which the dog is being left is a public dump or other facility
               designed for receiving such and has been designated by the board of commissioners
               as a public facility for receiving trash or refuse and the provisions of O.C.G.A.
               § 4-5-3 are complied with in full.

No person shall release a dog on any property, public or private, with the intention
               of abandoning the dog.

The state laws and regulations relating to the sale and distribution of alcohol in

(a) A license issued under this article shall be subject to all terms and conditions imposed

               and those under his supervision and control to report to the police department any

               which are in violation of this article or of state laws or the rules and regulations
               of the state revenue commissioner. (c) All licenses shall have printed on the front the following language: "This license is granted by the city council and accepted by licensee subject to all
               of the terms and conditions of the ordinances governing the issuance and retention
               of the same." (d) Each pouring licensee shall keep a copy of this chapter in the licensed restaurant
               and shall instruct any person working there in respect to the terms hereof and each
               licensee, the licensee's agents and employees selling, pouring or serving alcohol

questions.prompt: How many people make up the Gilmer County Board of Commissioners?
choices: A chairperson and one other member
A chairperson and two other members
A chairperson appointed by the governor
questions.answer: A chairperson and two other members
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Printed herein is 1995 Ga. Laws (Act No. 105), page 3824. Amendments to the Act are
               indicated by parenthetical history notes following amended provisions. Obvious misspellings
               have been corrected without notation. For stylistic purposes, a uniform system of
               headings, catchlines and citations to state statutes has been used. Additions made
               for clarity are indicated by brackets.

The terms of the commissioners of Gilmer County serving on the effective date of this
               Act shall end when the new commissioners elected pursuant to this Act take office. (1995 Ga. Laws (Act No. 105), page 3824, § 1)

(a) There is established in Gilmer County a board of commissioners, which board shall
               be the governing authority of said county and shall be composed of a chairperson and
               two other members to be elected by a majority of the qualified voters of the entire
               county voting in elections held for that purpose. All such elections shall be held
               and conducted as provided in O.C.G.A. § 21-2-1 et seq., the "Georgia Election Code." (b) The chairperson and other members of said board of commissioners shall have resided
               within Gilmer County at least one year prior to their election. The chairperson shall
               be at least 25 years of age prior to his or her election and the other members shall
               be at least 21 years of age prior to their election. (c) For the purposes of electing the chairperson and other members of said board, candidates
               for chairperson shall offer as candidates for that office, and there shall be two

questions.prompt: If a parking space on the street is marked with lines, how must you park?
choices: At least halfway into the space
Anywhere nearby as long as traffic is not blocked
Within the lines bounding that space
With two wheels on the painted line
questions.answer: Within the lines bounding that space
questions.excerpt:
Whenever a space is marked off on any highway for the parking of an individual vehicle,
               every vehicle there parked shall be parked within the lines bounding that space.

Commercial vehicles and trailers of all types, including travel, boat, camping and
               hauling trailers, shall not be parked or stored on any lot occupied by a dwelling
               or on any lot in any residential district except in accordance with the following
               provisions: (1) Not more than one commercial vehicle per family living on the premises, which does
                  not exceed one and one-half tons rated capacity, shall be permitted; and in no case
                  shall a commercial vehicle used for hauling explosives, gasoline or liquefied petroleum
                  products be permitted. (2) Not more than one camping or travel trailer, one hauling trailer, and one boat trailer
                  per family living on the premises shall be permitted and the trailer shall not exceed
                  33 feet in length, or eight feet in width; and further provided that the trailer shall
                  not be parked or stored for more than 48 hours unless it is located behind the front
                  yard building line. A camping or travel trailer shall not be occupied either temporarily
                  or permanently while it is parked or stored in any area except in a travel trailer
                  court authorized under this Code.

No person shall park a car on public property for the purpose of advertising it for
               sale.

It shall be unlawful for any railroad company, engineer, fireman, conductor or the
               employees of any railroad company to stop or cause to be stopped, any train or portion
               of train, car or locomotive, on or across any street crossing in the city for a longer
               period of time than five minutes at any one time.

It shall be unlawful for any motor truck or motor…

               of someone authorized by the owner to have custody of the animal. (b) When off the premises of the owner or custodian, such dogs, cats and other animals

               long. ( Ord. No. O-2022-1 , § 1(Att. 1), 6-21-2022)

In the construction of this Code, and of all ordinances, the following rules shall
               be observed, unless such construction would be inconsistent with the manifest intent

               committee of council that reviews the particular activity. Council, city council, mayor and council. Whenever the term "council," "city council" or "mayor and council" is used, it shall
               mean the mayor and council of the City of LaGrange, Georgia. County. The words "the county" or "this county" shall mean Troup County, Georgia. Gender. questions.prompt: Can a resident build a brick, wood, or other sidewalk in Locust Grove?
choices: Only with a written permit from the city
Yes if it matches the neighbor's sidewalk
Residents may not build sidewalks at all
questions.answer: Only with a written permit from the city
questions.excerpt:
Chapters:

Sections:

No sidewalk of any description shall be built by any individual, firm or corporation,
               of any brick, wood or other material without a written permit from the city. (Prior code § 4-1-6)

It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to drag or run, or cause
               to be dragged or run, any harrow or other implement, engine, machine or tool upon
               any asphalt, bithulitic, warrenite or other type of permanently paved street or sidewalk
               of the city which shall be liable in any way to injure or cut the surface thereof.
               It shall also be unlawful to injure any dirt street in the same manner. (Prior code § 4-1-7)

A. Use of public streets, alleyways, sidewalks, and roads of the city which blocks or
               impedes vehicular, bicycle, and/or pedestrian movement within the public right-of-way
               for extended periods of time shall not be permitted; unless permission has been granted
               by the mayor and city council as part of a special events permit. B. The placement of an object which blocks or impedes vehicular, bicycle, and/or pedestrian
               movement within the public right-of-way for extended periods of time in any portion
               of a public street, alleyway, sidewalk or road of the city shall be prohibited unless
               the mayor and city council specifically approve the use of such object as part of
               a special events permit. C. For use in this section, the phrase "block or impede" means to occupy the public right-of-way

questions.excerpt:
Retail licenses for the sale of malt beverages and wine in the county and permits
               for the wholesale distribution of malt beverages and wine in the county will be granted
               in the manner set out in this article. (Res. of 1-13-1998, § I)

Malt beverages and wine sold in the county may be consumed on the premises of the
               retailer if said retailer has an on-premises license. Malt beverages and wine will
               be sold by package only in retail businesses with an off-premises license. Malt beverages
               and wine may be refrigerated and cold prior to retail sale. Editor's note— In the referendum on May 24, 2016, [it was] voted in favor of distilled spirits being
                  sold as mixed drinks by the drink on the premises. (Res. of 1-13-1998, § II; Res. of 5-24-2016)

The retail licensee under this article must be a person of good moral character and
               a citizen of the United States. This shall not apply to the honorably discharged members
               of the nations' armed forces who have returned to the county within the prescribed
               limit. (1) The licensee shall not have been convicted within five years of the date of his application
                  of a felony or any violation of the laws of this state, or any other state, relating
                  to the sale of alcoholic beverages. (2) The licensee shall be the owner of the premises for which the license is held or the
                  holder of any lease thereon. (3) The licensee shall be active in, and solely responsible for, the management and operation
                  of the business for which the license is granted. (4) The applicant shall make a sworn statement of his qualifications according to the
                  requirements set forth in this section and shall place same on file with the county
                  clerk before any license is issued. (5) If the application covers a partnership, all members…

questions.prompt: After how many hours unattended without food, water, and shelter on the owner's own property is an animal considered abandoned?
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 12-08-20(B) , § 1, adopted Aug. 20, 2012, repealed the former Title 6, Arts. I—VI, and enacted
               a new Title 6 as set out herein. The former title pertained to similar subject matter
               and derived from Ord. No. 08-12-01, § 1, 12-1-2008. See also the Code Comparative
               Table for a detailed listing of repealed and added sections.

This title shall be known and may be cited as the City of McDonough "Animal Control
               Ordinance". ( Ord. No. 12-08-20(B) , § 1, 8-20-2012)

For the purposes of this title, the following definitions shall apply: Abandoned animal means any animal which shall have been placed upon public property or within a public
               building unattended and unsupervised or upon or within the private property of another
               without the express permission of the owner, custodian or tenant of the private property
               and is unattended or without care. Abandoned animal also shall mean any animal that
               has been upon or within the property of its owner or custodian for a period of time
               in excess of thirty-six (36) hours unattended and without adequate food, water and
               shelter. Adequate food means sufficient quantity of non-contaminated and nutritionally healthy sustenance
               that is appropriate to the species, breed, size, age and health of the animal, or
               at the direction of a licensed veterinarian, which is sufficient to prevent starvation,
               malnutrition, or risk to the animal's health. Garbage, spoiled, rancid, or contaminated
               food is not adequate food. Adequate shelter means a completely enclosed structure with four (4) sides with a door opening, a
               constructed floor, and a roof that is: A. Clean, dry and compatible with current weather conditions; B. Compatible with the age, size, species and condition of the animal;…

questions.prompt: What is the entire city of Midway designated as?
questions.excerpt:
(a) The rules and regulations of the county board of health, as amended from time to time,
               to the extent applicable within the city, with regard to animal control, are adopted
               and incorporated in this chapter by reference. A copy of all the adopted rules and
               regulations is on file in the office of the city clerk. Violations of the adopted
               rules shall constitute a violation of this chapter, subject to penalties as provided
               in section 1-6 . (b) Wherever a conflict exists between the adopted health department regulations and other
               provisions of this Code, the most stringent provision shall prevail and be controlling. (c) The municipal court shall have jurisdiction over violations of this chapter and procedure
               for enforcement of this chapter shall be as provided by state law. Complaints of violations
               shall be brought before the municipal court by designated representatives of the county
               board of health and shall be prosecuted through that court. A complaint shall be brought
               before the municipal court only after all notices and rights to a hearing before a
               hearing officer of the board of health shall have been provided. (Code 1955, § 9-3-4; Ord. of 2-12-1989)

(a) The entire area embraced within the corporate limits of the city is designated as

               to health or property in the opinion of the mayor and council, those birds may be
               destroyed as humanely as possible, under the supervision of the police department,
               in such numbers and in such manner as…

questions.prompt: What does Part I of Moultrie's city code contain?
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Part I of the Code of Ordinances, City of Moultrie, Georgia, consists of the Charter
               of the city, 1943 Ga. Laws, page 1458, as amended and supplemented by later laws. The material included has been rearranged under appropriate article headings, catchlines
               have been supplied for each section, some sections have been divided into subsections
               with catchlines, or divided into several sections, and each section has been given
               a Charter section number for the convenience of the user and for purposes of indexing.
               Each section contains in parentheses after the last sentence the official identity
               of the law from which it is derived and the section number thereof. There is included
               a comparative table with the Georgia Laws listed in this compilation arranged in numerical
               order showing opposite each section number the section number in this Charter. Also
               included is a comparative table of ordinances which have amended the Charter. Amended or repealed sections have been replaced or omitted, and supplemental laws
               have been placed under the relative article headings. The titles of all Acts, sections
               that have been executed or that are no longer effective, as well as the sections containing
               more legislative dicta are omitted. All Acts relating to the schools have also been
               omitted. Where an explanation seems helpful or an error in the language of the material is
               apparent, there is included an explanation or correction in brackets [ ]. For stylistic
               purposes, a uniform system of citations to state statutes has been used.

questions.answer: No, a city license is required for any alcoholic beverage
questions.excerpt:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcoholic beverage means a beverage which contains alcohol in any quantity or percentage, including,
               but not limited to, distilled spirits, liquor, beer and other malt beverages, wine
               and fortified wines defined by state law. Distilled spirits means any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 24
               percent alcohol by volume. License means the authorization by the city council to engage in the sale of alcoholic beverages. Licensed premises means one identifiable place of business consisting of one room or contiguous rooms
               wherein alcoholic beverages are sold or served under the same trade name and the entire
               building in which such room is or contiguous rooms are located (except that when such
               room is or contiguous rooms are located in a shopping center, hotel, motel, or similar
               facility or in a facility that houses more than one business under the same roof or
               in the same building or structure), then only such room and contiguous rooms and any
               adjoining storage, office, toilet, and other similar rooms shall constitute the licensed
               premises; however, any outside private patio area on private property that is actually
               and permanently attached to the room or to one or more of the contiguous rooms may
               be considered licensed premises for the purpose of serving alcoholic beverages from
               a bar or dispenser located within the room or contiguous rooms. The term "licensed
               premises" shall not include any parking lot, sidewalk, adjoining alley or lane, or
               any other area outside the interior of the licensed premises.…

Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Section 1, Att. A of an ordinance adopted Feb. 10, 2025 , repealed the former Ch. 6, and enacted a new Ch. 6 as set out herein. The former
               Ch. 6 pertained to similar subject matter and derived from an ordinance adopted Feb.
               2, 2009, att. A, §§ 30-101—30-115, 30-201—30-304, 30-401—30-408; and an ordinance adopted Mar. 6, 2017 , §§ 1, 5. State Law reference— Animals generally, O.C.G.A. title 4.

This chapter may be cited as the "City of Porterdale Animal Control Regulations." (Ord. of 2-10-2025(1) , § 1(Att. A))

It is the purpose of this chapter to minimize health hazards of animals, and to provide
               a healthier atmosphere in which the citizens may enjoy their pursuits and rights in
               their individual properties. (Ord. of 2-10-2025(1) , § 1(Att. A))

The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different
               meaning: Abandoned animal means any domestic animal or livestock unattended or not cared for in excess of 36
               hours. Adequate food means sufficient quantity of non-contaminated and nutritionally healthy sustenance,
               appropriate to the animal, or at the direction of a licensed veterinarian, sufficient
               to prevent starvation, malnutrition, or risk to the animal's health. Garbage, spoiled,
               rancid or contaminated food is not adequate food. Adequate shelter means protective cover appropriate for the species and adequate space to maintain
               the animal in good health and prevent pain, suffering or a significant risk to the
               animal's health. Adequate shelter shall consist of a completely enclosed structure
               with three to four sides with a door opening, a constructed floor, and a roof. Adequate
               shelter shall be clean, dry…

               as are required to be licensed by the county. (Res. of 9-2-1986)

Editor's note— An ordinance adopted March 4, 2002 repealed § 6-2, which pertained to Brown bagging

(a) No license for retail package sales of distilled spirits shall be granted to any person
               unless such person is of legal age, and (i) has been a resident of the county for
               a minimum of one year prior to filing an application for such license; or (ii) the
               application for such license is accompanied by a certificate of the Judge of the Probate
               Court of the county of the applicant's residence certifying that the applicant has
               been a bona fide resident of the county or municipality for at least 12 months immediately
               preceding the application and is a resident of a county or municipality where distilled
               spirits may be legally sold under this chapter. In either case, the applicant shall
               state on oath that he/she shall own for his/her own benefit, not less than 51 percent
               in the business which engages in such distilled spirits sales within Pulaski County,
               Georgia. (b) Person as used in this article shall include the licensee, his father, mother, brother,
               sister, son, daughter or the spouse of any such person or relation. (Ord. of 1-3-1978(1), § 1; Res. of 9-2-1980, § 2; Ord. of 4-2-2007(1))

Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Printed herein is 1996 Ga. Laws, page 3646, which created and established the city's
               recreation authority. Amendments to the act are indicated by parenthetical history

               are indicated by brackets.

This Act shall be known and may be cited as the "City of Richmond Hill Recreation
               Authority Act."

(a) There is created a body corporate and politic to be known as the City of Richmond
               Hill Recreation Authority, which shall be deemed to be a political subdivision of
               the State of Georgia and a public corporation by that name, style, and title and said
               body may contract and be contracted with, sue and be sued, implead and be impleaded,
               complain and defend in all courts of law and equity, except that the authority or
               the trustee acting under the trust indenture shall in no event be liable for any torts
               committed by any of the officers, agents, and employees. The authority shall not be
               a state institution, nor a department or agency of the state, but shall be an instrumentality
               of the state, a mere creation of the state, having a distinct corporate entity and
               being exempt from the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 50-17-20 et seq., the "Georgia State
               Financing and Investment Commission Act." The authority shall have its principal office
               in Bryan County, and its legal situs or residence for the purposes of this Act shall
               be Bryan County.…

State Law reference— Establishment of recreation systems authorized, O.C.G.A., Sec. 36-64-1 et seq.

The Mayor and Council may, by ordinance, establish reasonable rules and regulations
               covering the operation of the City's recreation and park facilities. When the rules
               and regulations are posted or displayed on the facility involved, such rules and regulations
               shall have the force and effect of law and any person committing any action in violation
               thereof shall be deemed to have violated this section and shall be punished as provided
               in § 1-1-8 of this Code.

(a) Park facilities are available on a "first come-first served" basis. (b) Groups wishing to reserve use of the park pavilion or community room may do so by
               contacting the City Hall. (c) No charge to the public may be made by any group using the community room. (d) Nonprofit groups wishing to use the park as part of a fund-raising activity may do
               so only after securing prior approval of the Mayor and Council. (e) No commercial use of the park shall be permitted.

questions.excerpt:
(a) Georgia Rules of the Road adopted. (1) Intent. The purpose of this section is to regulate traffic upon the public streets of the
               city and to repeal all other ordinances and regulations in conflict herewith. (2) Incorporation by reference. Per ch. 6 of tit. 40 of O.C.G.A. §§ 40-6-372—40-6-376 and §§ 40-6-1—40-6-395 of that
               chapter known as the Uniform Rules of the Road, and the definitions contained in O.C.G.A.
               § 40-1-1, are hereby adopted as and for the traffic regulations of the city with like
               effect as if recited herein. (b) Penalties. Unless another penalty is expressly provided by law, every person convicted of a
               violation of any provision of this section shall be punished by a fine of not more
               than $1,000.00 or by imprisonment of not more than six months or by both such fine
               and imprisonment. (Former § 8-001)

Parking limitations of certain areas of town. (1) Loading/unloading zones. The following are hereby designated loading/unloading zones in which parking shall
                  be limited to ten minutes: a. The alley running behind the stores on the west side of Cherokee Road; and b. The alley running behind the stores on the east side of Cherokee Road. (2) Handicapped permit parking. Only vehicles which have a current State of Georgia validly issued handicap permit
                  may park in areas designated as handicap parking. (3) "No parking" area. The following areas are designated as "no parking" areas are any area designated
                  as golf cart or motorcycle parking only parking spaces, or any places designated "no
                  parking." (4) Enforcement. All persons violating any provision of subsections (1), (2), or (3) will be guilty
                  of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction, may be punished by a fine not to exceed $100.00
                  per violation, each instance being considered a separate violation.…

questions.prompt: If South Fulton accepts and files your zoning application as an official document, what happens to the fee?
choices: You get half of it back
No part of the fee is returned

questions.answer: No part of the fee is returned
questions.excerpt:
This chapter shall become effective upon its adoption by the city council. All powers
               and authority granted by this chapter to the city's planning commission and city's
               zoning board of appeals shall be cumulative. Such powers and authority shall be in
               addition to all other powers and authority the planning commission and board of appeals
               now has or may later have under other laws. (Ord. No. 2018-047, § 1, 11-27-2018)

The policy for refunds of application fees in zoning matters will be as follows: (1) If the application is accepted and filed with the city as an official document, no
                  part of the application fee will be returned. (2) If the application is merely presented and returned to the applicant at his request,
                  or at the suggestion of the staff, before any entry is made upon any city record,
                  the full amount of the fee will be returned. (Ord. No. 2018-047, § 1, 11-27-2018)

The fees for filing of a zoning application with the county shall be as fixed from
               time to time by the city council. (Ord. No. 2018-047, § 1, 11-27-2018)

Subscription charges for mailing of zoning agendas shall be as fixed from time to
               time by the city council. (Ord. No. 2018-047, § 1, 11-27-2018)

               notice stating the nature of the violation and providing a reasonable time limit for
               the satisfactory correction thereof. The offender shall, within the period of time

Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Constitutional grant of home rule powers, Ga. Const. art. IX, § II; statutory grant

(a) Area embraced. The entire area embraced within the corporate limits of the city is hereby designated
               as a bird sanctuary. (b) Trapping, shooting, etc., birds or wild fowl; abatement of nuisance. It shall be unlawful to trap, hunt, shoot or attempt to shoot or molest in any manner
               any bird or wild fowl or to rob bird nests or wild fowl nests. Provided, however,
               if starlings or similar birds are found to be congregating in such numbers in a particular
               locality that they constitute a nuisance or menace to health or property in the opinion
               of the proper health authorities of the city, then in such event health authorities
               shall meet with representatives of the Audubon Society, Bird Club, Garden Club or
               Humane Society, or as many of said clubs as are to be found in the city, after having
               given clubs at least three days actual notice of the time and place of the meeting
               to the representatives of such clubs. (c) Destroying birds deemed nuisance. If, as a result of such meeting, no satisfactory alternative is found to abate such
               nuisance, then the birds may be destroyed in such numbers and in such manner as is
               deemed available by the health authorities under supervision of the chief of police
               of the city. (d) Penalty for violation. Anyone violating the provisions of this section shall be punishable by a fine of
               not more than $100.00 or imprisoned not exceeding 30 days. (Code 1988, § 4-2; Ord. of 10-4-1975)

Open burning means the burning of any materials wherein air contaminants resulting from combustion
               are emitted directly into the ambient air without passing through a stack or chimney
               from an enclosed chamber. For the purposes of this definition, a chamber shall be
               regarded as enclosed when, during the time combustion takes place, only such apertures,
               ducts, stacks, flues or chimneys as are necessary to provide combustion air and to
               permit the escape of exhaust gases are open. 1. Burning limited. a) Within the Town of Thunderbolt, the open burning of residential yard waste consisting
               of leaves and brush from vegetation grown on a residential property is permitted. i) The burning shall take place only from sunrise to sunset. ii) The burning of man-made materials such as paper, garbage, tires, shingles, plastics,
               lumber, and other kinds of wastes is prohibited. 2. Restrictions on burning yard waste. a) The burning of yard waste shall be conducted as follows: i) All fires must be at least 20 feet away from any building, structure or property line.
               At no time shall a fire be located on a town street, or property, unless specifically
               approved in writing. ii) Fire-fighting material sufficient to contain any fire started under this section will

(a) Purpose. The purpose of this ordinance is to provide guidelines for the issuance, approval,
               and fees associated with the granting of permits for filming by television companies,
               movie companies, or other media in the town. (b) Permit required. A film permit shall be obtained by any person working on behalf of television companies,
               movie companies, or other media, company or agency filming on town-owned property.
               For purposes of this ordinance, "town-owned property" includes, but is not limited
               to, town right-of-way. There shall be a consistent and uniform process for the issuance
               of film permits in the town. Any person planning a filming shoot which could impact
               public safety and/or disrupt town business is required to obtain a film permit. Failure
               to obtain a film permit shall be a violation of this section. Each day a film permit
               is not obtained shall be a separate violation. (c) Procedure for issuance of permits. (1) Application. a. Any person desiring to obtain a film permit shall make application to the town clerk

questions.prompt: For a place licensed to sell beer or wine in Whitfield County, what counts as adequate parking?
choices: One parking space for each 50 square feet of the building's floor area
One parking space for each 100 square feet of the building
One space for every employee plus customer spots
Whatever fits on the lot without blocking the street
questions.answer: One parking space for each 50 square feet of the building's floor area
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Public intoxication, § 10-3; adult entertainment, § 10-21 et seq.

For the purpose of this chapter, the following terms shall have the respective meanings
               ascribed to them: Adequate parking: One parking space for each 50 square feet of gross floor area of the building in
               which the licensee operates. Business area: Any street length between intersections where 50 percent or more is in use for business
               purposes. Business or commercial premises: Any public place to which the public is directly or impliedly invited during business
               hours for the purpose of purchasing goods, products, or services offered thereon or
               for the purpose of utilizing facilities located thereon. The term "business or commercial
               premises" shall include any semi-public place to which the public is directly or impliedly
               invited, whether or not a fee is charged for entry, and which does not otherwise qualify
               as a "bona fide private club" pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 3-7-1(1). Church: A permanent building where members and other persons regularly assemble for religious
               worship and which is publicly designated as a church, but shall not include a residence
               also used for religious purposes. College: Only such state, county, city, church or other colleges as teach the subjects commonly
               taught in the common colleges of this state, not to include private colleges where
               only specialized subjects such as law, stenography, business, music, art, medicine,
               dentistry, vocational occupations and other special subject are taught. Distance: The measurement in lineal feet, by the most direct route of travel upon the ground,
               from the front door of the structure from which malt beverages or wine is offered
               for sale, in a straight line to the nearest corner of…

This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the "Wilkes County Alcoholic Beverage
               Control Ordinance." (Ord. No. 01232012, § I, 1-23-2012; Ord. No. 06122014, § I, 6-12-2014)

The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meaning ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning. Alcohol means ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl, or spirits of wine, from whatever source
               or by whatever process produced. Alcoholic beverage means and includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, malt beverage, wine, or fortified
               wine as defined in this section, and beer. Bona fide private club means any nonprofit association organized under the laws of this state which: (1) Has been in existence at least one year prior to the filing of its application for

                  beyond a fixed salary. Calendar year means the period of time from the date of issuance of a license on or after…

questions.prompt: When is selling alcoholic beverages banned in Wrightsville?
choices: From 12:00 midnight Saturday until 6:00 a.m. Monday
All day on Sundays and holidays
From 2:00 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. each day
questions.answer: From 12:00 midnight Saturday until 6:00 a.m. Monday
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Alcohol, generally, O.C.G.A. title 3.

Except as otherwise provided by this Code, the terms used in this chapter shall have
               the same meaning as set forth in the Georgia Alcoholic Beverage Code, including the
               defined terms set forth in O.C.G.A. § 3-1-2.

Every licensee, including each retailer and wholesaler selling or delivering alcoholic
               beverages in the city, shall maintain full compliance with the Georgia Alcoholic Beverage
               Code, O.C.G.A. § 3-1-1 et seq.; no person shall commit any act prohibited by O.C.G.A.
               §§ 3-3-20 et seq. and 3-3-40 et seq.

No person shall sell alcoholic beverages between the hours of 12:00 midnight on Saturday
               nights (12:00 a.m. Sundays) and 6:00 a.m. on Mondays. During such times when the sale
               of alcoholic beverages is prohibited, any licensee whose place of business is open
               shall keep all alcoholic beverages locked up in a separate room, drink box, cooler
               or other such container.
